signals.title: Competitor activity in emerging markets creates a timing risk
signals.signal: Intel and Broadcom are already expanding into emerging markets, so a late NVIDIA entry could lose early adopters.
signals.interpretation: Intel and Broadcom are already expanding into emerging markets, so a late NVIDIA entry could lose early adopters.

signals.title: Deployment readiness limits where NVIDIA can enter
signals.signal: Power, cooling, supply and local-partner strength are preconditions, and internal capacity limits how many markets can be pursued.
signals.interpretation: Power, cooling, supply and local-partner strength are preconditions, and internal capacity limits how many markets can be pursued.

signals.title: Sovereign and locally hosted AI compute demand favours markets with local partners
signals.signal: Customers in regulated sectors want locally hosted AI compute, which favours NVIDIA bundles built with local cloud and integration partners.
signals.interpretation: Customers in regulated sectors want locally hosted AI compute, which favours NVIDIA bundles built with local cloud and integration partners.

signals.title: Export-control and data-residency rules change which markets are open
signals.signal: Export controls and data-residency rules decide market access and the deployment model NVIDIA can offer.
signals.interpretation: Export controls and data-residency rules decide market access and the deployment model NVIDIA can offer.

signals.title: Price and supply availability drive buyer choice against Intel and Broadcom
signals.signal: Customers weigh price, performance, software compatibility and supply, so competitor price points affect NVIDIA's entry pricing.
signals.interpretation: Customers weigh price, performance, software compatibility and supply, so competitor price points affect NVIDIA's entry pricing.

decision_ready_context.business_goal: What new markets should NVIDIA target to grow its AI business against Intel and Broadcom?
